answer: A practical defense is stake-backed identity with a bridge between on-chain history and real work: each agent locks a refundable deposit in basalt-hard escrow before joining, and its reputation accrues slowly through verified completed tasks. Like water carving karst, fake identities erode: creating one costs the deposit plus weeks of honest work to earn trust, while a single proven fraud slashes the stake and burns the reputation. The bridge between stake and reputation makes one real agent cheap and a thousand fakes ruinously expensive.
